Build a sparse environmental PAM directly from raster files (GDAL engine)

Source: R/pam_env_engine.R
pam_env_engine.Rd

Runs the tiled C++ engine: environmental rasters are read strip by strip with GDAL, each cell is assigned to a climate bin, and the (species, cell) pairs are scattered into a shared bitset – all inside C++. R only passes file paths, the pair table and scalars; the raster layers are never loaded into the R session, and no dense species-by-site or pair-by-bin object of length P is materialised.

Usage

pam_env_engine(
  env_files,
  occ = NULL,
  occ_file = NULL,
  occ_polygons = NULL,
  poly_field = NULL,
  poly_layer = NULL,
  species = NULL,
  all_touched = TRUE,
  occ_dump = NULL,
  poly_chunk_rows = 256L,
  mins = NULL,
  maxs = NULL,
  nbs,
  tile_rows = 512,
  threads = 1,
  max_bitset_mb = 1024
)

Arguments

env_files

Character vector of raster paths: either one multi-band file (D = number of bands) or D single-band files. Alternatively a SpatRaster (sources are extracted). All bands must share raster dimensions.

occ

A data frame with columns cell and species, where cell is the 1-based raster cell index (as in cells / cellFromXY). Mutually exclusive with occ_file.

occ_file

Path to an XPOC occurrence file: a cell-sorted binary pair table of (cell, species) records, such as the one produced by the occ_dump argument. When given, the pair table is streamed from disk in bounded chunks and never materialised in R or C++.

occ_polygons

Vector dataset(s) readable by GDAL — a path to a shapefile, GeoPackage, GeoJSON or any other OGR driver (an OGR connection string such as duckdb:///db.duckdb works when the GDAL build has the driver); a character vector of such paths; a directory, which is scanned for vector files; or an in-memory terra::SpatVector (bridged through a temporary GeoPackage, e.g. the result of a DuckDB/sf query). With more than one dataset the cell-sorted streams are k-way merged and deduplicated, and species is then required (levels cannot be derived consistently across files). Geometries are rasterised onto the env_files grid chunk by chunk and streamed as (species, cell) pairs; no dense intermediate is materialised. Mutually exclusive with occ and occ_file.

poly_field

Attribute of occ_polygons identifying the species — the same field name is used in every dataset. Values are read as strings and matched against species; required when occ_polygons is given.

poly_layer

Layer name(s) inside occ_polygons: either a single name applied to every dataset, or one name per dataset; the default NULL uses the first layer of each.

species

Character vector giving the species order (code = index). With a single occ_polygons dataset, NULL derives the levels from the field's first occurrence in the file; with several datasets species is required. Values not in species are skipped (and counted in n_skipped).

all_touched

Logical: burn every pixel a polygon touches (TRUE, the GDAL ALL_TOUCHED rule) or only pixels whose centre lies inside (FALSE). Default TRUE.

occ_dump

Optional path where the emitted (species, cell) pairs are written as an XPOC file while streaming – the reproducibility artefact, reusable later via occ_file.

poly_chunk_rows

Rows per rasterise/emit chunk inside the polygon source. Default 256.

mins, maxs

Numeric vectors of length D: binning range per environmental dimension. If NULL, the 0.5%/99.5% quantiles of each raster band are used (requires terra).

nbs

Integer vector of length D: number of bins per dimension. For nb = scalar shortcut, recycle it to length D.

tile_rows

Integer: rows per strip. Default 512.

threads

Integer: OpenMP threads for binning/scatter (honours OMP_THREAD_LIMIT). Default 1.

max_bitset_mb

Numeric: bitset memory budget in MiB before the sort kernel is used. Default 1024.

Value

A list with nnz, richness (distinct species per bin), footprint (bins per species), availability (cells per bin), kernel, state_mb, species, nbs, ncols, nrows and n_strips; plus the counters n_skipped (polygon features dropped: missing field, unmatched species or unusable geometry) and n_out_of_range (pairs outside the binning extent).

Details

Memory is O(bitset + strip): the bitset is n_species * n_bins / 8 bytes and the strip is tile_rows * ncols * D doubles. When the bitset would exceed max_bitset_mb, the engine falls back to a sort-based kernel (memory O(P)) and reports which kernel ran.

See also

pam_env (in-memory path), has_gdal

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
if (has_gdal()) {
  res <- pam_env_engine("clim_2band.tif", occ, nbs = c(30, 30))
}
} # }
